Because it shares libraries with Creative Cloud, assets from Photoshop or Illustrator can be used directly in Express projects, and designers can hand off a template that colleagues then adjust.

item.title: BestPhotoAI
item.description:
BestPhotoAI is meant for fast photo improvement. A user uploads an image, and the tool can sharpen details, increase resolution, fix lighting and color, and retouch skin, then returns an enhanced version. The aim is to save time compared with manual editing in Photoshop or Lightroom.

Typical users are e-commerce sellers who need clean product photos, creators preparing profile and social images, and people restoring older pictures. Automated enhancement works best on ordinary issues like low light or noise, and results vary with the source image.

item.title: ClipDrop
item.description:
Clipdrop packages common image edits into simple web tools. Remove Background cuts out a subject in a click, Cleanup erases unwanted objects, Image Upscaler enlarges small pictures with added detail, and Uncrop extends an image beyond its borders. Relight changes the lighting on a subject, and Replace Background swaps in a new scene from a text prompt. A text-to-image generator rounds out the set, using Stability AI models.

Product photographers, e-commerce sellers, marketers, and casual users reach for it when they need a quick edit without opening a heavy editor. The tools work in the browser and on mobile, with an API for developers who want to add the same features to their own apps. The project had a short stint under Stability AI before moving to Jasper, which acquired it to expand its marketing tools.

item.title: Erase.bg
item.description:
Erase.bg handles one of the most common editing jobs. You upload a picture of a product, person, or object, and an AI model detects the foreground and removes the background, producing a PNG with transparency. It works on people, products, animals, and cars, and handles complex edges like hair reasonably well. Typical users are online sellers, designers, and anyone making a profile picture or a presentation.

Several features make it more practical for volume work. Batch processing lets you upload many images at once, and an API and plugins integrate with design tools and workflows. After removing the background, you can add a solid color, a new image, or leave it transparent. A free tier gives low-resolution results, and paid credits or subscriptions unlock high-resolution downloads.

item.title: Fotor
item.description:
Fotor covers everyday editing for people who do not want Photoshop. In the photo editor, you crop, adjust color and light, apply filters and effects, and retouch portraits by smoothing skin and removing blemishes. A collage maker and a design studio offer templates for social posts, posters, and cards. Everything works in a browser, with matching apps for phones and computers.

AI tools handle the harder steps. One-click enhancement improves exposure and sharpness, background removal makes cutouts, an object remover erases distractions, and an upscaler enlarges small pictures. Newer features include text-to-image generation, avatars, and generative fill for extending or changing parts of an image. Fotor also has an AI video editor for simple clips.

item.title: Galileo AI
item.description:
Galileo AI was one of the early tools for turning a prompt into interface designs. You described a screen, such as a fitness app dashboard or a checkout page, and it produced a detailed, editable design with components, imagery, and layout, which could be copied into Figma and refined. It was popular with product designers and founders as a way to explore ideas and get past the blank canvas.

Google acquired Galileo AI and brought its team and technology into its own design-generation product, Stitch, which creates interfaces from text or images and exports to Figma and code. The standalone Galileo service was wound down as part of that move.

item.title: InstaWebAI
item.description:
InstaWebAI generates a full website from a short brief. A user enters information about the business, and the tool creates pages, copy, images, and a structure designed for search engines, which can be edited and published. The goal is to cut the time from idea to live site to minutes.

It targets owners who lack design or writing skills and want a professional baseline. Typical outputs include home, services, about, and contact pages, along with metadata for search visibility. Publishing options and domain connections vary by plan.

item.title: Khroma
item.description:
Khroma starts by asking you to pick 50 colors you like. A neural network learns your tastes from those choices, then generates an endless stream of color combinations that match your style, shown as palettes, gradients, typography samples, and images. The aim is to make exploring color feel personal instead of random.

Designers use it to find inspiration for brand identities, websites, and illustrations. You can save favorite palettes, view them in different layouts, check color contrast, and search for combinations by a specific color. The interface is minimal and focused on discovery, and everything runs in the browser.

item.title: Luminar Neo
item.description: Luminar Neo is built for photographers who want strong results without a lot of manual work. Instead of slider-heavy workflows, it offers AI tools that do the hard parts in a click. Sky AI replaces or enhances skies, Relight AI changes the lighting in a scene using depth information, Portrait Bokeh AI creates background blur, and tools for skin, face, and body adjustments handle portraits. Generative tools can erase objects and expand the canvas.

item.title: MagicSlides
item.description:
MagicSlides speeds up deck creation. A user enters a topic, pastes text, or uploads a document, and the tool builds slides with titles, bullets, and images. Because it works as an add-on inside Google Slides and PowerPoint, the results land in a familiar editor for refinement.

It supports many languages and offers themes and layouts. Students use it for assignments, and professionals use it to produce a first draft of a presentation, which they then edit. Images can be sourced automatically.

item.title: Meshy
item.description:
Meshy makes 3D asset creation fast. You type a description or upload an image, and it generates a 3D mesh with textures in a minute or two. The results can be rotated, refined, and downloaded in common formats. Indie game developers, 3D printing hobbyists, product designers, and virtual world builders use it to produce props, characters, and environment pieces without modeling each from scratch.

The platform includes tools for the steps after generation. It can retexture a model from a prompt, remesh to adjust polygon counts and topology, and add skeletons and animations to characters. Plugins and an API connect it with Blender, Unity, Unreal Engine, Maya, and other tools, so assets can flow into existing pipelines. A library of community models provides starting points.

item.title: Outfit.fm
item.description:
Outfit.fm addresses the cost of fashion photography. A seller photographs a garment on a hanger or flat, uploads it, and the tool generates images of the item on virtual models in settings that suit the brand. Options include different body types, poses, and backgrounds.

Small brands and online sellers use it to fill catalogs and social feeds without booking models, studios, and photographers. Speed lets them test styles and update visuals frequently.

item.title: Photoroom
item.description:
Photoroom grew from a background remover into a full product photography tool. Take a picture of a product on a table, and the app cuts it out cleanly, then places it on a white background, a color, or an AI-generated scene with realistic shadows and lighting. For small sellers on marketplaces like Etsy, eBay, and Shopify, that means professional-looking listings without a studio.

Other features expand the range. An AI backgrounds tool creates settings from a text description, an instant shadow and relight tool adds depth, and a magic retouch removes objects and blemishes. Templates in standard sizes speed up posts for social media and marketplaces. Batch editing handles whole catalogs, and an API lets platforms add the same processing to their own apps. Teams can share brand templates.

item.title: Pixlr
item.description:
Pixlr offers editing in a browser without installing software. Pixlr E is a more advanced editor with layers, masks, and adjustment tools that resemble Photoshop, while Pixlr X is a simpler editor for quick fixes, collages, and templates. It opens common image formats, including PSD files to an extent, and works on desktop and mobile browsers.

AI features handle the hard parts. Background removal makes cutouts in a click, an object eraser removes distractions, generative fill and expand add or extend content from a prompt, and automatic enhancement and retouching improve photos. An AI image generator and tools for creating designs from templates broaden what it can do. Pixlr is part of the Inmagine group, which also offers stock content.

item.title: Remove.bg
item.description:
Remove.bg made background removal fast and easy. You upload a photo, or drag it onto the page, and an AI model detects the foreground and returns the image with a transparent background in a few seconds. It handles people, products, animals, and cars, and it copes reasonably well with difficult edges like hair and fur. It is used for e-commerce product photos, profile pictures, ID photos, and design mockups.

The service extends beyond the website. Plugins connect it to Photoshop, Figma, and other tools, apps let you process images on a phone or desktop, and an API allows platforms to add automatic background removal at scale. Once the background is removed, you can add a solid color, a template, or another image. Bulk tools handle large catalogs. Remove.bg is owned by Canva.

item.title: Tripo3D
item.description:
Tripo focuses on speed and consistency. Enter a description or upload an image, and it generates a 3D model in seconds to a minute, with options for style and level of detail. The models are meant to be usable in games, animation, 3D printing, and e-commerce, and the platform provides downloads in common formats like GLB, FBX, and OBJ.

Features go beyond the initial generation. Tools can create cleaner topology for animation, generate or replace textures from a prompt, add skeletons so characters can be posed, and apply animations. A segmentation option separates a model into parts for editing. An API and integrations with Blender, Unity, Unreal, and other applications fit it into creative pipelines, and a community library offers starting points.

item.title: Uizard
item.description:
Uizard is a design tool built for speed and accessibility. You can upload a photo of a sketch or a screenshot of an existing app and have it converted into an editable design, or describe a screen in text and let the AI generate a layout. A library of templates, components, and themes helps non-designers build presentable prototypes for products, websites, and apps.

Collaboration features let teams comment and iterate, and prototypes can be linked into clickable flows. An Autodesigner feature creates multi-screen designs from a prompt, and the AI can generate color themes from an image. It’s popular with founders, product managers, and consultants who need quick mockups to communicate ideas.
